title: FACT CHECK: Claire Castro not appointed SC justice
summary: Castro remains with the Presidential Communications Office and has denied applying for the position of Supreme Court associate justice

blocks.text: Claim: Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro has been appointed as a Supreme Court (SC) associate justice.
Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube channel named “PINAS BALITA TV,” which has over 176,000 subscribers, posted the claim on November 4.
The video is titled, “Hala! Grabe ito! May bagong ma-appoint as Supreme Court Justice? Ante Kler lang ang sakalam dito!”
(This is intense! Someone new is being appointed as Supreme Court justice? Auntie Claire is the only strong one here!)

The video’s thumbnail shows an image of the Palace press officer wearing a judicial robe with other SC justices in the background. Text on the thumbnail claims she has been appointed and promoted to the high bench.
Another video, posted on October 28, bears a thumbnail image of Castro wearing a judicial robe with the text, “USec Claire sa Supreme Court?”
Several social media users expressed surprise at the supposed appointment, with some questioning her credentials.
As of writing, the November 4 video has garnered over 5,300 views and 284 likes.

The facts: Castro continues to serve as Palace press officer and PCO undersecretary. In fact, she has held several press briefings after the misleading video was posted, with the most recent one held on November 15.

While Castro is a lawyer, she explicitly denied applying for a judicial post when asked to comment on reports about her supposed appointment as SC associate justice. In a media briefing on October 27, Castro addressed speculation that she might be appointed to the High Court following reports that then-associate justice Rodil Zalameda was a top contender for the chief justice post, potentially opening up a vacancy for associate justice.
“Associate justice ng Supreme Court si ‘Ante Kler’? Hindi ako nag-apply. So, wala pong katotohanan ‘yun.” she said.
(‘Ante Kler’ as an associate justice of the Supreme Court? I didn’t apply. So, that’s not true.)
She added that she would not preempt President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in choosing the next chief justice.
On November 6, Marcos appointed Zalameda as the 28th chief justice of the country. He succeeds former Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who retired upon reaching the mandatory retirement age of 70.
Constitutional qualifications and process: Under Article VIII, Section 7 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, a candidate for the Supreme Court must meet the following qualifications:

items: Must be a natural-born citizen of the Philippines
Must be at least 40 years of age
Must have been a judge of a lower court or engaged in the practice of law in the Philippines for at least 15 years

blocks.text: Moreover, under Article VIII, Sections 8 and 9 of the Constitution, the President can only appoint members of the Supreme Court from a list of at least three nominees prepared by the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) for every vacancy.

Because Castro did not apply for the position, she was not on the JBC shortlist and could not have been legally considered or appointed to the High Court.Unrelated video content: The video itself does not provide any proof of Castro’s supposed appointment.

Instead, it features the narrator reacting to a news site’s social media posts involving Castro and Vice President Sara Duterte. He enumerates the qualifications required to become a Supreme Court justice and claims to assess whether Castro is eligible, yet fails to present any evidence that she was allegedly nominated or appointed.
Debunked: Rappler has debunked other false claims involving Castro:

FACT CHECK: Claire Castro quote blaming heavy floods on blocked drains is fake
FACT CHECK: Claire Castro quote on Marcos’ plans to run for VP is fake

blocks.text: Rappler has also fact-checked false claims originating from the same YouTube channel:

items: FACT CHECK: Lacson remains a senator, did not resign
FACT CHECK: No reports of SC order ousting Marcos
FACT CHECK: No report of Indonesian President confronting, scolding Marcos

blocks.text: – Lyndee Buenagua/Rappler.com
Lyndee Buenagua is a Metro Manila-based journalist who primarily covers Bicol and Baguio. She is also an alumna of Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.
